points.heading: One-word verb times
points.body:
A verb is an action word (cantar = to sing). To conjugate means to change the verb for who speaks (I, you, he/she) and for when the action happens. Indicative is the mood we use to tell facts as real.

A simple tense = the verb is ONE word. Five to know: present = now/habit (canto); imperfect = ongoing/past habit (cantaba); preterite = finished past (canté); future = later (cantaré); conditional = would (cantaría).

Stem = what is left after dropping -ar/-er/-ir (cantar → cant-). Ending = the tip you add. Changing the ending also changes the time.

I-forms of cantar: canto / cantaba / canté / cantaré / cantaría.

Práctica: Write the five I-forms for cantar and comer. Label each: now / ongoing past / finished past / later / would.

Error común: Using cantaba for a fully finished «yesterday» event. Use canté.

points.heading: Two-word verb times
points.body:
A compound tense = TWO words. Word 1: a helper form of haber (he, has, ha…). Here haber does not mean «there is»; it is only a helper. Word 2: the participle = the «already done» form, usually ending in -ado or -ido (cantado, comido).

Example: he cantado = helper he + participle cantado («I have sung»). The participle stays the same for I/you/he; only the helper changes.

Práctica: Write he / había / habré / habría + cantado. Circle the helper and underline the participle.

Error común: Writing hemos comidos (plural -s on the participle). Correct: hemos comido.

points.heading: One word or two?
points.body:
Ask: is it a clear finished moment (usually ONE word) or an «already done» result with haber (TWO words)?

Examples: «Ayer terminé» (one word, closed yesterday) frente a «Ya he terminado» (two words, result still matters).

Práctica: Make three pairs (one-word vs two-word) with the same verb. Explain each choice in one short line.

Error común: Using two words with a closed «ayer» when your home variety expects one word (fui).

lesson.summary: Learn to say WHEN an action happens: one-word forms (canto, cantaba, canté…) and two-word forms (he + cantado), and when to choose each.
